article.articleSummary:

Uganda has interrupted transmission, but the DRC continues to experience spread amid insecurity, population displacement, strained health systems, and community mistrust, hindering surveillance and case management. There is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo. The outbreak is a key backdrop to a UN Human Rights Council session in Geneva, with calls to strengthen multilateral cooperation for health. article.articleHeadline: Doc Talk | Dengue Can Affect The Brain And Nerves: Watch Out For These Warning Signs
article.articleSummary: Dengue can involve the brain and nerves, causing neurological manifestations such as encephalitis, encephalopathy, acute seizures, transverse myelitis, and Guillain-Barré syndrome. Warning signs warranting neurological evaluation in current or recent dengue or flu-like illness include severe, persistent headaches; confusion or disorientation; excessive drowsiness; a seizure; new weakness; and difficulty walking, balancing, or speaking. Early assessment matters, as Guillain-Barré can progress over days and outcomes improve with prompt intervention before respiratory or autonomic involvement. No dengue-specific antiviral exists; management is supportive—hydration, treating the underlying infection, and close monitoring. Prevention relies on vector control, early diagnosis, and awareness across emergency departments and clinics. In July 2026, India’s CDSCO approved the first dengue vaccine—a live, attenuated tetravalent vaccine given in two doses three months apart for ages 4–60—yet it complements, not replaces, vector control or immediate protection this monsoon.

article.articleHeadline: Vaccination, screening, and prevention: Gastroenterologist Dr Anurag Sachan's guide to beating hepatitis
article.articleSummary: Dr. Anurag Sachan of Paras Health Kanpur outlines vaccination, screening, and prevention for hepatitis in India. Screening is crucial: HBsAg and anti-HCV tests, with CDC recommending one-time screening for 18–79. Prevention includes safe injection practices, screened blood products, harm reduction, safe sex, avoiding unsterile tattoos/piercings, and public health measures for clean water and sanitation to prevent HAV. Antivirals control HBV; DAAs often cure HCV; early diagnosis and follow-up remain essential.

article.articleSummary: Nearly 4,000 dengue cases reported across West Bengal as of 7 September 2026, with Kolkata intensifying transmission after a three-day 'Cleanliness Welcome' dengue elimination drive. Hotspots include Tollygunge, Kasba, and New Alipore; fever clusters are prominent in Shyambazar, Hatibagan, and Shobhabazar. Authorities say door-to-door fever surveys will be conducted through mid-October, and anyone with fever lasting two days or more and dengue-like symptoms should be referred to a health facility. In Kolkata, Ward 2 records 35 fever cases; Ward 9 (Alipore, Ekbalpur, Chetla, Mominpur) 31; Ward 10 shows the highest mosquito larvae at 326 sites across areas including New Alipore, Tollygunge, Kasba, Rath Tala, Dhakuria, Gariahat, Lake Gardens, and Tollygunge Victory Garden. Ward 11 has 217 larval sites; Ward 14 has 146. Investigations identified 76 construction sites with standing water, 56 vacant plots, and 28 waterlogged ponds; breeding sites include discarded ice-cream cups and tires.

article.articleHeadline: E. coli presence in bottled water in Keralam's Kochi points at need to ensure water traceability
article.articleSummary: E. coli and coliform bacteria were detected in bottled drinking water in Kochi, Kerala, prompting contamination-control measures and a push for water traceability. Most probable number (MPN) values ranged from 17 to 1,600 per 100 ml, with zero MPN expected in drinking water. To improve safety, the Kochi Corporation plans to mandate hotels use only Kerala Water Authority (KWA) water, enabling source tracing via a QR code linked to the My Kochi app. A stakeholder meeting will be held to trace water sources and take action. Contamination was found during surprise checks by the Health Department, Kochi Corporation, Food Safety Department and police. While routine checks have not always shown E. coli in bottled water, officials will focus more on cans; a Kalamassery-area fungal-growth complaint is under test. KHRA notes ISI-marked bottled water is used; tracing water sources remains essential.

article.articleHeadline: Moringa and Salmonella: What It Is, Why It Keeps Getting Contaminated, and Whether There Is a Common Source
article.articleSummary: Five Salmonella outbreaks linked to moringa leaf powder—one in 2015–2016 and four since 2025—have caused 219 illnesses and 59 hospitalizations, with at least 11 recalls since November 2025. Moringa oleifera leaves are dried into powder used in lactation products and green-powder supplements; a 2016 FDA finding tied the outbreak strain to organic moringa powder in RAW Meal, with the exporter placed on Import Alert 99-19. By October 2025, traceback pointed to Vallon Farmdirect PVT LTD of Jodhpur, India (batch VFD/ORG/MORP/L/24). In January 2026, 131 cases across 38 states prompted FDA to cite a common Indian manufacturer behind Live it Up and Why Not Natural, though it did not name the supplier. February Rosabella could not determine a source, though a single supplier was recalled; May MOGO traced mostly to one supplier. Recall activity spans Oct 2025–Sept 2026. Drying of moringa leaf powder—often open-air—facilitates Salmonella contamination in dried botanicals.

article.articleHeadline: Record-breaking tests; malaria control remains a challenge.
article.articleSummary: Despite record malaria testing in Mumbai, malaria control remains a challenge. In 2025, the Mumbai Municipal Corporation expanded screening to 1,889,012 blood samples, yielding 10,163 malaria cases. The annual blood examination rate (ABER) rose to 14.5%, exceeding the long-standing 12% target, yet the annual parasite incidence (API) climbed from 0.3 (2022) to 0.5 (2023), 0.6 (2024), and 0.8 (2025), signaling ongoing transmission. Historical ABER hovered around 11.3–12.1% since 2015, with 2024 at 11.7%. In early 2026, 761,439 samples were tested, and 3,394 were positive. Experts caution that increasing tests alone won’t curb malaria; effective vector-control, timely diagnosis and treatment, and rapid action on transmission sources are essential to reduce API. Data surfaced via RTI activist Chetan Kothari from Mumbai authorities. Location focus: Mumbai, India; disease: malaria; key metrics: ABER, API, case counts, and testing trends.

article.articleHeadline: Balaghat News: Balaghat: Risk of infection from water-logged open plots; action taken is merely a token gesture.
article.articleSummary: Balaghat, Madhya Pradesh, India reports rising infection risk from water-logged open plots around residential areas due to poor drainage. Rainwater has filled plots into ponds with residents observing toxic organisms in the stagnant water, raising concerns of infections among locals. No effective action has been taken; plot owners remain unidentified, hindering enforcement. Areas affected include Narmada Nagar, Budhi, Bhatera, Devtola, Bypass Road, and Saraswati Nagar, where cleanliness and drainage have deteriorated. Authorities have previously carried out only token measures. Residents urge immediate identification of plot owners and active drainage clearance to mitigate health risks. The situation underscores governance gaps and urgent public health concerns from unattended water accumulation in Balaghat city.

article.articleHeadline: Sivaganga health authorities deploy medical camps to contain fever outbreak in villages
article.articleSummary: As of 7 September 2026, an eight-year-old girl died of suspected influenza in Kattunedungulam, Sivaganga district, Tamil Nadu, after fever developed last week; she was a third-grade student at Kattunedungulam Government School and died on arrival at a government hospital following private treatment. Three additional children in the village and several adults have fever and missed school/work. Health authorities launched medical camps near Kattunedungulam, distributed treatment, and collected blood samples from children; sanitation drives with disinfectants were conducted in coordination with the local panchayat. Medical teams were also dispatched to the neighboring village of Sundaranadappu after reports of viral fever spreading there. District Health Officer Meenakshi confirmed preliminary tests indicate the deceased child was infected with influenza virus, while investigations continue into possible underlying conditions. Other children remain in stable condition, and containment measures are ongoing.

article.articleHeadline: Howrah reels under dengue attack, cases touch 115
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Howrah rose to 115 cases this week from 94, signaling ongoing transmission but still below last year’s level. The spike is tied to alleged poor coordination between the district health department and Howrah Municipal Corporation (HMC) health wing. CMOH Kishalay Dutta accused HMC OSD Ashutosh Kundu of non-compliance with Swasthya Bhavan directives, potentially widening infection pockets. Residents complained of testing-kit and medicine shortages and selective testing, while Kundu reportedly urged staff to conserve kits and test only high-fever patients. Dutta denied shortages and said Swasthya Bhavan supplies as needed; Kundu was unavailable for comment. A senior HMC official denied the allegations but admitted staff shortages, deficient data collection, and irregular larvicide spraying by VBD/VCM workers. HMC plans drone-based larvicide spraying in high-incidence areas. District magistrate P. Deeppappriya will review persistent problems as MLAs criticized spraying, drain-cleaning, and data gaps in dengue-control efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Increase in Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease Among Children
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease is rising among children in Tamil Nadu, India. The illness is caused by Coxsackievirus A16; Enterovirus 71 can cause more severe disease. The current outbreak is mild, mainly affecting children under 5. Symptoms include fever, sore throat, mouth and tongue ulcers, and blisters or red patches on the hands, feet, and trunk; dehydration, vomiting, diarrhea, headaches, and loss of appetite may occur. It spreads easily between children via saliva, respiratory droplets, and contaminated fluids. Most children recover within about a week. Prevention tips include keeping affected children home for a week and cleaning the school if a case is identified; hygiene measures such as wiping children with water twice daily are advised. No cause for undue alarm.aution-backed awareness and basic hygiene are encouraged.

article.articleHeadline: M'laya's pig trade faces ASF question
article.articleSummary: ASF outbreaks in Meghalaya, India, are examined in a Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology study covering July 2020–April 2025, with 115 outbreak events affecting 1,603 pigs in seven districts and direct losses around Rs 2.74 crore. Ri Bhoi and East Khasi Hills reported the most outbreaks; both districts are key pig-movement corridors. Meghalaya imports live pigs from Assam, Haryana, Punjab, Karnataka, Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Mizoram to meet demand. Movement of animals, people and vehicles, notably via NH-6 to Assam, is cited as a potential spread factor. The study does not prove imported pigs caused outbreaks, and the first outbreak’s source remains unknown, but calls for enhanced surveillance, entry-point testing, quarantine, and stronger biosecurity in movement hubs. ASF does not infect humans but threatens livelihoods and pork availability; better checks are needed to trace sources and prevent spread.

article.articleHeadline: Number of fever patients in Kerala rising sharply: More than ten thousand people sought treatment just yesterday | news
article.articleSummary: 8 September 2026: Kerala reports a sharp rise in fever and vector-borne diseases. Yesterday, 10,943 people with fever sought care in government hospitals, Malappuram recording the highest at 2,496. In September, 73,679 patients have been treated so far. Beyond fever, dengue (31 confirmed yesterday) and chikungunya (12 confirmed yesterday) are spreading; this month dengue has reached 432 cases with one death. Districts reporting fever cases include Thiruvananthapuram 678, Kollam 388, Pathanamthitta 415, Alappuzha 518, Kottayam 235, Idukki 282, Ernakulam 890, Thrissur 1,036, Palakkad 965, Kozhikode 937, Wayanad 514, Kannur 732, Kasaragod 857. Higher temperatures and climate change are believed to boost mosquito populations. Health officials face criticism for sanitation and vector-control lapses; urgent containment measures are urged to curb breeding and transmission. Hepatitis A is also a concern in the state.

article.articleHeadline: Buying seafood contaminated with poisonous crabs could trigger a major disaster; during crab season, beware these marine toxins.
article.articleSummary: Crab season warning highlights a squid dish contaminated with a tiny red-spotted crab carrying tetrodotoxin, a deadly neurotoxin; high heat cannot destroy it. This and related crabs can harbor toxins, with distribution across Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, East Africa, and China’s Guangdong and Hainan. Toxins include tetrodotoxin and paralytic toxins; symptoms start with numbness of lips and extremities, gait instability, and may progress to respiratory failure. Spoiled seafood can harbor Vibrio parahaemolyticus. Other hazardous marine life listed include toxic shellfish, the woven snail that accumulates tetrodotoxin and paralytic toxins, the heart cowry, blue-ringed octopus, and box jellyfish. Practical safety tips: avoid unfamiliar seafood, buy from reputable markets, keep raw and cooked items separate, ensure thorough cooking to at least 100°C for several minutes, and limit raw intake for the elderly, children, pregnant women, and those with weak digestion.

article.articleHeadline: U.S. pork exports fall in July due to Aujeszky's disease.
article.articleSummary: U.S. pork exports in July fell to 224,305 tonnes (−6% YoY) and $641.8 million (−6%), after restrictions tied to Aujeszky’s disease found in pig viscera. Restrictions were lifted mid-to-late July, but monthly results remained weak. Exports rose to Japan, Central America, Colombia, and Canada, yet declined to Mexico (which rebounded in July but stayed below year-ago levels as production resumed) and to China, Korea, Oceania, and the ASEAN region. The per-head carcass value was $62.53, below the prior year but $3 above June. Through July, year-to-date shipments reached 1.73 million tonnes valued at $4.86 billion, up ~2% in volume and ~1% in value versus the same period last year, keeping annual pace above 2025. USMEF president Dan Halstrom credited lifting the viscera restrictions as critical, noting China’s earlier stricter inspections creating delays, which have been resolved.

article.articleHeadline: Opening of seven new schools and a rubella vaccination campaign in Luxor.
article.articleSummary: Luxor Governorate prepares for the 2026/2027 academic year with seven new schools entering service, delivering 111 classrooms as part of expansion, replacement, and refurbishment of existing facilities. The seven campuses span Qurna, Esna, Al-Tod, Armant, Beiya, and Al-Zinia, including Nag Hassan Primary (Qurna) with 7 rooms; Esna Secondary Vocational (15); Al-Adisat in Al-Tod (12); Khaled bin Al-Walid in Al-Dobaya, Qurna (16); Al-Hurriya Primary in Armant (12); Al-Nasr Preparatory in Beiya (30); Al-Hurriya Primary in Al-Zinia (19). Administrative handover has been completed and equipment procurement finalized prior to school start. On the health front, Luxor Health Directorate is launching a three-week national vaccination campaign against measles and rubella targeting Egyptian and non-Egyptian children within the specified ages, with teams deployed outside clinics to centers, mosques, churches, and community sites. Public awareness campaigns via media and loudspeakers will facilitate access to remote areas. The governor urged coordinators to remove obstacles to ensure a smooth, safe school opening.

article.articleHeadline: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria that are not affected by antibiotics detected in migratory bird droppings in Hokkaido, Setsunan University and others.
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant Stenotrophomonas maltophilia was detected in droppings from migratory great black-backed gulls breeding in Akkeshi, Hokkaido, that travel between Hokkaido and East Asia, by a team including Setsunan University; findings were reported in a U.S. scientific journal by September 7, 2026. The bacterium, known to cause pneumonia and bloodstream infections in immunocompromised individuals and linked to severe COVID-19 outcomes, showed resistance to two antibiotics commonly used against it. Genetic analyses indicated some strains possess traits that help them evade drugs via protective membranes and enhanced motility. Several detected strains are of types not previously reported in Japan, suggesting possible introduction from overseas. The gulls are omnivorous and forage widely, potentially acquiring bacteria from diverse environments. The researchers argue that antibiotic resistance issues should account for migratory birds in cross-border spread and surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: National Key R&D Program team rushes to Wulan, Qinghai, to bolster the plateau's zoonotic disease prevention and control network.
article.articleSummary: Nine-member team from China’s National Key R&D Program on Monitoring, Early Warning and Integrated Control of Major Zoonoses visited Wulan County, Haixi Prefecture, Qinghai, Aug 27–28, 2026, to bolster plateau zoonotic disease prevention. Leveraging an integrated demonstration base, they coordinated with the county CDC, Animal Epidemic Prevention Center, and local authorities, outlining 2026 monitoring tasks and technology promotion. Fieldwork in Kekex Town’s Nansha Gou Village and Shirigou Town collected 200 animal samples, 80 high-risk human samples, and 30 food samples to trace Brucellosis and Tuberculosis, with attention to Anthrax and Echinococcosis. Community outreach educated herders on prevention, early detection, and treatment; distributed over 100 educational materials and 150 bottles of doxycycline hydrochloride. The team hosted the Colorful Wulan lecture series and the ZhiHui Wulan talent session, and on Aug 28 submitted findings and preventive measures to county leaders to support green, organic livestock production and disease control efforts on the plateau.

article.articleHeadline: One Contaminated Kitchen, Thousands of Children Poisoned
article.articleSummary: September 2024 in Tuscany, Italy saw a centralized school catering outbreak: Salmonella enterica serovar Strathcona ST2559 contaminated cherry tomatoes caused 224 cases and 26 hospitalizations; three Qualità & Servizi officials faced investigation for hygiene neglect. The same risk chain appears in Japan’s Yashio (June 2020): a single supplier’s lunch program for 15 schools sickened 2,958 of 6,732; E. coli O7:H4 carrying astA traced to fresh salad ingredients, including red alga Gigartina tenella. Germany, September 2012, reported about 11,000 gastroenteritis cases across 390 institutions linked to a single lot of frozen strawberries from China; 22 tons prompted a recall of 1,136 boxes, with the RKI estimating prevention of ~11,000 further cases. Tokyo, 2017: four norovirus outbreaks in 10 schools affected 4,209 people, 1,193 symptomatic; kizami nori seaweed from one producer carried norovirus GII.17 with matching genomes. Toyama, Japan, June 2021: >1,800 people across 25 schools affected by milk from one factory; pasteurization reportedly at 128°C.

article.articleHeadline: A 5 cm-long parasite hid in her brain for seven years! A woman's drinking of unboiled mountain spring water triggered the disaster.
article.articleSummary: Guangxi, China: A 56-year-old woman developed intracranial cysticercosis after seven years of progressive neurological decline. Beginning in 2017 with facial droop, gait instability, and slurred speech, she was repeatedly misdiagnosed as stroke or brain tumor until 2019 when intracranial parasitic infection was confirmed. Over subsequent years she suffered headaches, right‑sided numbness, and later left‑leg weakness with worsening balance; speech deteriorated. In August, imaging and cerebrospinal fluid tests supported cysticercosis, and doctors performed an awake craniotomy to remove a 5 cm parasitic worm. The operation successfully extracted the worm. Family history notes she lived as a farmer and drank unfiltered stream water and mountain spring water without boiling until around 2015. Doctors warn that consuming raw water and undercooked meat are major routes of cysticercosis, which can cause chronic brain inflammation, edema, and progressive neurological injury, even death.

article.articleSummary: Flu activity surges among children in the Gyeonggi-Incheon region as autumn weather arrives, with daily highs dropping below 30°C since late last month. In Suwon, a pediatric clinic tested 39 for influenza last Saturday, about 30% positive (roughly 13 cases). Similar crowding was reported at pediatric facilities in Dongtan City and Incheon, where clinics were crowded and feverish children wore masks. Nationwide sentinel surveillance shows rising influenza-like illness: in week 35 (Aug 23–29), 13.3 per 1,000 outpatients had influenza-like illness, up from 9.2 previously and 6.4 in the same period last year. Age distribution peaks at 7–12 years (36.5 per 1,000), followed by 1–6 years (22.6 per 1,000). The Gyeonggi-do Education Office has issued guidance urging home-based prevention; COVID-19 activity is also observed.

article.articleHeadline: Why does the opening of Water Margin begin with a great plague and the 'Temple of Subduing Demons'? (Image)
article.articleSummary: Water Margin opens with a major plague in the Northern Song capital, Dongjing, in spring 1058 (Jiayou 3). Emperor Renzong’s early relief efforts fail, prompting Chancellor Fan Zhongyan to summon the Dragon-Tiger Mountain Celestial Master to perform rites to dispel the calamity. Envoy Hong Xin reaches the sealed Temple of Subduing Demons and releases 108 demon lords—36 Tian Gang and 72 Earth Fiends—foreshadowing the Liangshan heroes. The article explains qi (prayer) and reng (exorcism) as a traditional unity of heaven and governance, rooted in Tianren gan ying. The imperial response includes grand rites (Luo Tian Da Jiao), reduced meals, halted music, amnesty, and pilgrimages to temples; folk practices such as nuó and city-god processions persist. Medicine and ritual coexist: Zhang Zhongjing’s Shang Han Za Bing Lun; Sun Simiao’s pharmacopeia; Song’s Anle Fang and Anji Fang; Su Dongpo’s Hangzhou Anle Fang, funding hospitals and providing free care, later nationalized. The opening ties plague to governance, faith, and medical care.

article.articleHeadline: The sky has fallen! It's full of hundreds of millions of bacteria! Every household uses it every day—don't stay in the dark! Take a look now!
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-09-07, routine kitchen items harbor massive bacterial loads and can raise risks of acute gastroenteritis and related symptoms. German microbiology studies and Chinese CDC data show a dishwashing sponge used for a week can contain hundreds of billions of bacteria per cubic centimeter, with more than 300 species present; kitchen cloths may total hundreds of billions. Wooden cutting boards with deep knife marks trap residues and moisture, hosting billions of bacteria plus mold and mycotoxins. Common culprits include Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Salmonella; molds like Aspergillus can produce persistent mycotoxins inside wood. Bamboo or wooden chopsticks and damp chopstick holders concentrate bacteria at the root ends. Mop heads retain moisture and foster microbes. Recommendations: replace sponges every 2–4 weeks, use separate boards for raw meat and produce, dry items thoroughly, wash cloths weekly or monthly, and consider disposable wipes to reduce cross-contamination.

article.articleHeadline: West Nile virus, an old antifungal slows the virus in the brains of mice: miconazole opens a new pathway.
article.articleSummary: A decades-old antifungal, miconazole, inhibits West Nile virus replication in neuronal cells and partially protects mice from fatal brain infection, according to a July 21, 2026 study by researchers at Shanghai's Naval Medical University and published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. In a screen of 722 FDA-approved compounds capable of crossing the blood–brain barrier, miconazole achieved near-complete inhibition of West Nile virus at 20 μM, with modest effects on cell viability; it also showed dose-dependent activity against yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis, and tick-borne encephalitis viruses in vitro. In vivo, ten mice intracerebrally inoculated with lethal WNV and treated orally with 50 mg/kg/day for five days survived 66.7% versus 0% in controls, with lower brain viral loads and less weight loss. Silencing TXNL1 (thioredoxin-like protein 1) reduced infection; overexpression increased replication, implicating TXNL1 as a host factor. Limitations include the artificial infection model and immediate treatment; human applicability requires pharmacokinetic/safety data and clinical trials.

article.articleHeadline: A girl puts on new shoes, suddenly develops a persistent fever of 39°C; she is taken to hospital and found to have a systemic infection! This is a habit many people have.
article.articleSummary: In Zhejiang, China, a pediatric patient (alias Xiaohua) at Zhuji City People’s Hospital in early 2026 presented with two days of fever (39.3°C) and leukocytosis. Initial symptoms were fever and mild cough; a crucial clue appeared when clinicians found a bandage over the left heel from a new-shoe blister, not changed for several days. Wound inspection revealed a developing abscess under the adhesive; after incision and drainage, the fever subsided that afternoon. Bacterial culture identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) as the pathogen, explaining progression to a systemic infection. MRSA is common in children and can enter via skin wounds, especially when bandages are used in closed, damp environments. The case highlights rapid pediatric infection progression and the need for careful wound care. The article also dispels four band-aid misconceptions and outlines proper use: cleaning, appropriate size, correct placement, daily changes, and safe removal.

article.articleHeadline: Mainland Chinese man with enlarged lymph nodes suspected of tuberculosis; doctor asks, "Have you had contact with cats?" to identify the real cause.
article.articleSummary: A 43-year-old man from Henan province presented with progressive neck lymphadenopathy. Pathology showed granulomas and two TB-related tests (PPD and T-SPOT) were positive, initially leading clinicians to suspect tuberculous lymphadenitis. In Wuhan, clinicians reviewed exposure history and asked about contact with cats, especially wild cats. After genetic testing, the diagnosis was Bartonella henselae infection, known as cat scratch disease, not tuberculous lymphadenitis. Following symptomatic treatment, the wound and enlarged nodes gradually improved. Cat scratch disease is transmitted among cats by fleas; humans can become infected after a cat scratch, bite, or licking of broken skin, and cats may be asymptomatic. Physicians emphasize including animal contact history in persistent lymphadenopathy with fever, with treatment decisions depending on symptom severity and whether other organs are involved.

article.articleHeadline: Guangdong Rotavirus Peak Season Approaching; Experts Urge First-Time Parents to Seize the Vaccination Window - Hong Kong Commercial Daily.
article.articleSummary: Rotavirus in Guangdong, China, is entering a prolonged autumn-winter peak season, with double peaks: a small peak in Oct-Nov and a peak from Dec to Feb, potentially extending to April. Officials urge first-time parents to vaccinate within a strict window of 6 to 32 weeks after birth, administering three oral doses. Rotavirus remains the leading cause of diarrhea in children under five; globally diarrhea is the second-leading cause of death in under-5, with about 35% of rotavirus diarrhea deaths. Transmission is fecal-oral, with possible respiratory droplets and close contact; R0 is second only to measles. There is no specific antiviral; management relies on rehydration and zinc. Four oral vaccines are available in China (one imported, three domestic). P[8] genotype is most associated with hospitalization. Emphasis on combining multiple vaccines to reduce clinic visits; vaccination should be prioritized due to climate-related risk increases in Guangdong.

article.articleHeadline: Avian influenza surveillance in poultry environments and pneumonia patients
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza viruses continue to circulate in China's poultry-human interfaces despite vaccination and culling reducing H5 and H7 lineages. A two-year surveillance (Dec 2021–Dec 2023) in three cities collected environmental samples from live poultry markets, slaughterhouses, and farms, alongside 840 respiratory specimens from hospitalized pneumonia of unknown etiology (PUE). Real-time RT-PCR tested 8,335 environmental samples for influenza A and subtype assays for H5, H7, H9, and H10. Overall, 32.2% were influenza A positive; H9 dominated at 20.1%, H5 at 7.1%, H10 at 0.2%, and H7 was not detected. Autumn and winter had higher positivity for H5 and H9. Rates were higher in live markets and slaughterhouses than farms/backyards. H5 showed no significant difference across sample categories, while H9 had a higher median positive rate across categories. Findings indicate persistent, low-level viral circulation at the human-animal interface, with ongoing clade 2.3.4.4b H5 presence.

article.articleHeadline: Five types of cancer can be prevented with vaccines; see which diseases are related to viruses and bacteria.
article.articleSummary: Persistent infections by HPV, hepatitis B, and other agents are linked to about 10% of cancers. Vaccines against HPV and HBV are safe, effective, and part of Brazil’s SUS; the HPV vaccine has been in the National Immunization Program since 2014. HPV types 16/18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers; INCA projects 19,310 new cervical cancer cases in Brazil in 2026. Cervical cancer is the third most incident cancer among women, with higher burden in the North and Northeast due to access gaps. A Lancet Global Health study (2019–2023) in 20–24-year-olds found HPV vaccination associated with a 58% reduction in cervical cancer incidence and a 67% reduction in CIN3. The SUS adopted DNA-HPV testing for screening in 2024, with 2025 guidelines favoring primary testing; cytology remains during transition. HPV is also linked to cancers of penis, vagina, vulva, anal canal, and oropharynx, mostly after 60; oropharyngeal cancer is more common in men. HBV transmission via blood/fluids and perinatal exposure; chronic HBV increases risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria is concentrated in the Amazon and exposes health inequalities.
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains highly concentrated in Brazil’s Amazon region, where over 99% of cases are reported. In 2025, Brazil recorded 118,037 malaria cases and 39 deaths, with transmission linked to Anopheles mosquitoes in rural, riverside, and Indigenous communities near borders. The infection highlights health inequities and limited access to services; delayed diagnosis and treatment sustain transmission. Since 2024 the SUS has offered tafenoquine (single-dose) to prevent relapses, alongside expanded diagnostics, testing, and treatment. Diagnosis is by simple blood test; hallmark symptoms include high fever, chills, sweating, severe body aches, and headache 8–30 days after a bite. Environmental factors—higher temperatures, humidity, deforestation, and forested areas—boost vector survival. Cross-border movement from Venezuela, Colombia, and Peru raises risk; cases can be imported or autochthonous, with Anvisa guiding investigations when autochthonous transmission occurs. Prevention relies on nets, suitable clothing, and repellents, plus rapid care access.

article.articleHeadline: Researchers from USP create an 'intelligent' vaccine that is safer against Chikungunya.
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya vaccine: Researchers from the University of São Paulo (USP) with German collaborators developed an 'intelligent' vaccine using a genetically modified Chikungunya virus that can replicate only once, training the immune system to produce antibodies without causing disease. In initial mouse tests, a single dose protected the animals, indicating a novel vaccine platform that could be adapted to other diseases. Published in npj Vaccines, the work contrasts with the current live-attenuated Chikungunya vaccine, which FDA approved in 2025 after a suspension but with restrictions: not indicated for very young children, elderly, immunocompromised, or those with certain comorbidities due to adverse effects. The Brazilian-German collaboration highlights a potential safer approach for Chikungunya and related pathogens as of 2026-09-07.

article.articleSummary: Parasitic infection risk in Brazilian skipjack tuna: Researchers from the Federal University of Santa Catarina, Brazil, examined 53 skipjack tuna caught in southern Brazilian waters and found parasites in 96% of them (about 51 fish). The 1,600 parasites were mainly in the gut, with numerous also detected in edible flesh; kidneys and heart were parasite-free. Ingesting parasite-contaminated or undercooked tuna can cause nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. To prevent parasites moving from intestines to meat, the study advocates promptly gutting fish immediately after capture. Because parasites are not readily visible, freezing at −20°C or colder for a specified period before consuming raw fish, or ensuring thorough cooking to the center, is recommended. The findings concern tuna used for sashimi, canned tuna, and tuna flakes and stem from southern Brazil.

article.articleHeadline: A study links deforestation to Chagas disease and leishmaniasis in the interior of Acre
article.articleSummary: Deforestation in Cruzeiro do Sul, interior Acre, Brazil, is linked to altered vector behavior for Chagas disease and leishmaniasis. In a study of 20 sites across a rural settlement, researchers compared preserved versus cleared landscapes. For Chagas disease, triatomine bugs infected with Trypanosoma cruzi were found in palm trees near homes, indicating that vegetation loss brings natural transmission foci closer to residents and raises contact risk. For leishmaniasis, Nyssomyia antunesi sandflies dominated collections, with abundance tied to how long and how extensively an area has been occupied and modified by humans, allowing persistence even where forest remains partly intact. In Cruzeiro do Sul, cutaneous leishmaniasis averages about 3 cases per 10,000 inhabitants per year, causing skin ulcers that can affect the nose and mouth in some cases. The findings suggest deforestation reshapes interactions among vectors, wildlife, and people, increasing transmission potential; a 2025 study noted degraded Amazon areas also raise malaria risk.

article.articleHeadline: Electronic tongue can detect avian influenza in 6 minutes; understand
article.articleSummary: Electronic tongue, a multisensor platform developed by researchers at the University of São Paulo, detects antibodies against avian influenza (Influenza A H5N1) in about six minutes. It can track regions and species with prior exposure, enabling early outbreak detection and containment for clinical and veterinary use. The device, built at the IFSC (Institute of Physics of São Carlos) and published in Applied Nano Materials, uses plant-derived proteins—zein (corn), jacalin (jackfruit), and concanavalin A (ConA; from hog bean)—and sericin to modify gold nanoparticles. It measures electrical properties, with sensor responses forming a pattern that identifies substances in the sample. While promising, tests used commercial anti-H5N1 antibodies and fetal bovine serum enriched with these antibodies; human blood samples have not yet been tested. Calibration and durability challenges may be mitigated by artificial intelligence, and scale-up to thousands of devices must remain low-cost and reproducible.

triage.headline_ja: 電子舌が6分で鳥インフルエンザを検出できる可能性、その仕組みを解説
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は新規検出技術（電子舌センサー）に関する研究開発報道であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイクの発生を報告するものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Minister of Education cancels schedule in Minas Gerais due to an outbreak of human scabies.
article.articleSummary: Alfenas, in southern Minas Gerais, Brazil, faces a scabies outbreak with more than 150 cases since late August. The Ministry of Education (MEC) canceled a visit by Minister Leonardo Barchini to Alfenas, including labs at Centro de Biologia Experimental (Cebioex) and the Center for Drug Prospecting in Fármacos, Fitofármacos e Novas Tecnologias (Profatec), as well as a visit to Unifal-MG’s Dentistry facilities and a World Literacy Day event at Escola Municipal Tereza Paulino da Costa. In the municipal network, about 50 cases have been confirmed among students and staff across five schools, with two daycares (Cemeis Dona Zinica and Dona Vanja) accounting for most cases. Preventive actions include school suspensions, cleaning, and guidance. A city committee was formed; the Sept 7 parade was suspended. At the prison, cases occurred about three months ago; none are symptomatic now. An Aug 28 meeting coordinated health, education, sanitation, epidemiology, and prison officials.

triage.headline_ja: 教育大臣、疥癬(ヒト疥癬)の集団発生によりミナスジェライス州での日程をキャンセル
triage.triage_reason: 疥癬という比較的軽症の感染症だが、150例超の集団発生により教育大臣の視察中止や市の対策委員会設置など社会的・行政的関心が高まっているため、WPRO基準複数該当かつ社会的関心ありでピックアップ対象とする。
triage.notes: 疥癬は通常重症度が低いが、学校・保育所での集団発生と行政対応（大臣の日程キャンセル、パレード中止、対策委員会設置）が社会的関心を高めており、続報の監視が推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: Meningitis case pulls CMEI out of parade in Cascavel.
article.articleSummary: One confirmed case of meningococcal meningitis in a four-year-old in the Cataratas neighborhood led Cascavel authorities to pull CMEI Doce Infância from the Sept 7 civic parade on Avenida Brasil as a precaution. Health officials activated a sanitary blockade, providing preventive medications and monitoring 48 children and staff who had contact with the patient. The infected child remains under specialized medical care; no additional school-community cases were reported over the weekend, and active school surveillance continues. Meningococcal meningitis is a rapid-onset bacterial infection; symptoms include high fever, neck stiffness, and headaches, prompting early diagnosis. Authorities emphasize vaccination and updated vaccination records, and have set up a hotline and on-call service for families.

triage.headline_ja: 髄膜炎感染例により、カスカベルのCMEIがパレードから除外
triage.triage_reason: 単発の髄膜炎菌性髄膜炎症例であり、封じ込め対応（予防投薬・監視）が既に実施され、他の症例報告もないため、国際的懸念や社会的関心の拡大は認められない。
triage.notes: 地域(Mato Grosso do Sul)が発生地域として記載されているが、記事本文はカスカベル（パラナ州）の単発例に関する内容であり、ブラジル全体としての公衆衛生上の重大性は認められない。対象国リストにブラジルは含まれるが、単発の学校内感染事例でありシグナルとしての基準を満たさない。

article.articleHeadline: India Approves the First Dengue Virus Vaccine.
article.articleSummary: India approves Takeda’s dengue vaccine Qdenga, the first dengue vaccine in the country, with rollout possible next year. Over the past five years, India has reported more than 1 million dengue cases, though real figures may be higher, driven by tropical climate and Aedes mosquitoes breeding in standing water after monsoon rains. While vector-control efforts continue, experts say wide vaccination could significantly reduce hospitalizations (80–90%); if integrated into the National Immunization Program, which currently covers more than 26 million newborns annually, vaccine impact would be amplified. Estimated import price ranges from $35 to $70 per dose. For poor families, access remains uncertain; Delhi resident Kailash notes affordability is critical, while Niraj, 18, in a northern slum, emphasizes equitable access beyond wealth. The vaccine is already included in Brazil’s national program, and authorities expect it to help India address a high-demand, crowded urban setting.

triage.triage_reason: デング熱ワクチンの承認に関する政策的なニュースであり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事態ではないため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事はデング熱ワクチン承認という保健政策ニュースであり、感染症アウトブレイクの探知ではない。ブラジルは既存プログラムの参考例として言及されているのみで、発生地域としての主題ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Malawi passenger intercepted with dried rodents, 10kg raw beef at Chicago airport
article.articleSummary: Malawi passenger intercepted at Chicago O'Hare International Airport with more than two pounds of dried African rodents and 22 pounds of raw beef in luggage during routine inspection. Federal agents confiscated and destroyed the items under US agricultural biosecurity rules to prevent introduction of infectious diseases. The passenger's identity has not been released, and no criminal charges have been filed. The seizure underscores restrictions on bushmeat and wildlife products, enforced by CBP, USDA, and CDC to reduce the risk of pathogens such as Ebola. In a similar case last year, a traveler arriving at O'Hare from the Democratic Republic of Congo carried four pounds of wild monkey meat, 11 pounds of insect-infested beans, and 17 pounds of unregistered plant material; these items were confiscated and destroyed, and the traveler was fined $300 after claiming unawareness of import restrictions.

article.articleHeadline: MSF Ebola response: Testimony from a nurse
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) with more than 6,000 confirmed cases and over 3,000 deaths, declared a little over three months ago. MSF nurse Martina Marchiò describes the human toll behind the numbers, including 64-year-old Jean Louis, a teacher who lost his wife and two daughters; his youngest daughter, aged 20, died days later. A tiny pink coffin seen on a roadside personalizes the tragedy. Symptoms noted include diarrhea, weakness, and bleeding. Frontline realities are stark: heat inside a yellow protective suit, meticulous hand-washing, and a constant risk of infection from a single lapse. Beyond medicine, the piece stresses community trust, psychological support, prevention, and clear communication. MSF calls for global mobilization of funds and resources to treat the sick, protect healthcare workers, prevent new infections, and reach remote communities in the DR Congo.

triage.headline_ja: MSFのエボラ対応：看護師の証言

article.articleHeadline: Child health: cholera — a call to protect millions of children in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Cholera severely affects children in Africa, with 44% of cases under 10 years in the Central African Republic; in Chad nearly two-thirds of infections are under 15; in Cameroon the median patient age is 10. The outbreaks span six countries, driven by seasonal rains, population movement and floods that contaminate water sources and damage sanitation infrastructure. Since Jan 1, 2026, Nigeria reports over 50,000 cholera cases and 338 deaths. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, over 30,400 cases and about 700 deaths, the highest death toll among affected countries. UNICEF warns the epidemic is no longer border-limited, moving along shared river basins and trade routes, endangering millions of children. Transmission concentrates along two corridors: the Lake Chad basin (Chad, Cameroon, Nigeria) and the Congo Basin (DRC, Republic of the Congo, RCA).

article.articleHeadline: Mourning in Cape Verde, exodus in Nigeria, Ebola in the DRC: Africa faces a new series of crises - Cameroun24.net infos actus news
article.articleSummary: Cabo Verde reports a bus crash on Fogo island that killed 25 people, including 12 children, with 12 children hospitalized; two days of national mourning declared and flags at half-mast after what authorities call the archipelago’s deadliest road accident this century. In Katsina State, Nigeria, residents of at least 15 villages in the Dandume district have fled amid intensified Boko Haram/ISWAP-linked attacks, with more than 100 civilians abducted in two weeks and disruptions to farming and trade. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola response faces violence and distrust; at least 45 aid workers were subjected to 76 incidents in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu, including assaults and arson against clinics. Community burial practices and suspicions toward outsiders complicate surveillance and may fuel transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Tuesday inauguration of the Ebola treatment center in Kisangani - ACP
article.articleSummary: An Ebola Treatment Center (ETC) in Kisangani, capital of Tshopo Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, is scheduled to be inaugurated on Tuesday, 8 September 2026, after completion in record time funded by donors. The facility, located in the Plateau Medical neighborhood in Makiso commune, was visited by members of the risk communication for community engagement (CREC) who confirmed the construction is finished. Donatien Kalonji stated details would be provided at the inauguration ceremony. The article notes the ceremony will be held with provincial authorities leading the event. The development marks a key addition to Ebola response infrastructure in northeastern DRC, though no outbreak specifics or case counts are provided.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Ituri: Large-scale training is necessary to strengthen community relays - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola remains in Ituri province, North-East Democratic Republic of the Congo, prompting a push for large-scale training to empower religious and community actors as effective population relays for prevention. Mgr Wilfried Banga of the Africa Inland Church in Bunia advocates expanding training beyond a limited group to reach more religious and community leaders who can disseminate prevention messages within their networks, citing ongoing ignorance and the persistent health threat. Religious leaders are seen as key mobilizers capable of broadening outreach through regular church and community presence. Emphasis is placed on continuing preventive measures: thermoflash temperature checks, regular handwashing, physical distancing, and avoiding close greetings and large gatherings. Sensitization should persist as long as the threat endures, with active participation from churches and community structures. Partners are encouraged to sustain support for training to extend reach to more people.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ州のエボラ：地域社会の連携役を強化するための大規模な研修が必要 - ACP

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Personal protection against the epidemic, a major factor in safeguarding the community (A notable) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Isiro, North-East Democratic Republic of Congo (Haut-Uele), 7 September 2026: A Haut-Uele notable stresses personal protection against Ebola as a key safeguard for the community. Baltazar Anga urges individual responsibility and strict adherence to preventive measures, including not touching corpses, and calls youths to abandon risky habits. He emphasizes Ebola as a form of sanitary insecurity for families and urges respect for state health rules. Amid armed robberies and ADF incursions, he advocates strengthened collaboration among provincial authorities, security services, and residents to restore peace. He also condemns rogue soldiers and stresses unity to defeat both the Ebola epidemic and the rising insecurity threatening daily life in Isiro.

article.articleHeadline: Be vigilant for influenza and RSV in patients with cardiovascular disease.
article.articleSummary: Influenza and RSV infections markedly affect patients with cardiovascular disease. Fever, tachycardia, dyspnea and hypoxia can destabilize heart failure and coronary artery disease. WHO notes higher severity risk for influenza in people with chronic conditions; RSV infection raises hospitalization risk in those with pre-existing heart disease. A NEJM study shows the first seven days after influenza confirmation carry about a sixfold higher risk of hospitalization for acute myocardial infarction; a JAMA Network Open study reports increased cardiovascular events after RSV, especially among those with CVD. Vaccination and infection control are essential: the American Heart Association endorses annual influenza vaccination for coronary artery disease and includes vaccination in heart failure care. In Vietnam, the Vietnamese Respiratory Society advises RSV vaccination for people 60+, especially with heart disease, after assessment. World Heart Day health program, Sep 18, 2026, at Ho Chi Minh City University of Medicine and Pharmacy Hospital.

article.articleHeadline: Enterovirus-related visits exceed 8,000 in a single week after schools reopen; outbreak expected to continue rising.
article.articleSummary: Last week in Taiwan, enterovirus activity remained high after schools reopened, with ED/clinic visits over 8,300—up 17% from the prior week—and officials warn the outbreak may continue rising; whether weekly visits exceed 12,000 (the epidemic threshold) remains under watch. Enterovirus D68 drives most severe domestic cases, second only to EV71 in risk. Seven severe cases have been recorded this year, including five D68, one Coxsackie A4, and one A16, with one death. D68 commonly causes fever, runny nose, and cough, but can progress to pneumonia, encephalitis, acute flaccid weakness, and rare respiratory failure. No vaccine or specific antiviral exists; prevention centers on thorough soap-and-water handwashing (10–20 seconds) and avoiding crowded places. Children under 5 are high-risk. Nearby Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore are rising; Korea has peaked and declined; Vietnam nears 100,000 cases this year with 10 deaths. Severe signs include drowsiness, confusion, limb weakness, seizures, persistent vomiting, rapid breathing, or tachycardia—seek hospital care.

article.articleHeadline: 4-year-old boy with a persistent 40°C fever, adenovirus infection detected.
article.articleSummary: Adenovirus infection causing persistent high fever in a 4-year-old boy from Ninh Bình, Vietnam, treated at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases in Hanoi. The child had 2 days of fever up to 40°C with sore throat, poor appetite, vomiting, and mild cough; exam showed red throat and bilateral tonsillar pseudomembranes. COVID-like? No—viral test confirmed Adenovirus; C-reactive protein was mildly raised; chest X-ray showed no pneumonia. Managed with fever control, fluid replacement, and supportive care; fever subsided after 5 days, symptoms improved, and the patient was discharged on day 7 after two afebrile days. Clinicians caution against judging severity by fever alone; monitor temperature, overall condition, appetite, and breathing. Transmission occurs via respiratory secretions, direct contact, hands, and contaminated objects; emphasize hand hygiene and avoiding shared items. Advise rest, adequate fluids, appropriate antipyretics, and prompt medical care for persistent high fever, lethargy, poor intake, rapid breathing, or hypoxia.

article.articleHeadline: Denmark: Gonorrhea cases rise among men who have sex with men, 3 Ceftriaxone-resistant cases detected
article.articleSummary: Denmark reported 5,134 gonorrhea cases in 2025, with 3,747 among men and 1,387 among women; 343,224 test episodes were completed. Incidence continues to rise among men who have sex with men (MSM) while heterosexual transmission stabilizes. In 2025, the country of infection was known for 4,013 episodes (78%), and 8% were acquired abroad, largely in Spain, Germany, Thailand, Sweden and the United Kingdom; men had a higher abroad-acquisition proportion (10%) than women (5%). By orientation, MSM abroad accounted for 9-10%. Twelve cases involved female-to-female transmission. Gonorrhea was detected at 20 non-traditional sites (eyes, joints, blood). Ceftriaxone-resistant gonococci were found in two men infected in Southeast Asia in 2025 and a third in January 2026; sources include Cambodia and Vietnam. No further spread of these resistant strains has been detected in Denmark; all three were treated with ceftriaxone without treatment failure, and DNA analyses show unrelated strains.

triage.headline_ja: デンマーク：男性間性交渉者（MSM）における淋病症例が増加、セフトリアキソン耐性株3例を検出
triage.triage_reason: デンマーク国内でMSMを中心に淋病症例が増加しており、東南アジア渡航関連のセフトリアキソン耐性淋菌（薬剤耐性菌）が複数例検出されたため、公衆衛生上異常な事象として注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Many new malaria cases detected in Khanh Hoa Province; doctors advise on what needs to be done.
article.articleSummary: Malaria cases detected in Khanh Hoa Province through screening: from Aug 17–31, 1,310 at-risk individuals were tested, with 18 confirmed positive for malaria due to Plasmodium. The province's CDC says two communes, Nam Khanh Vinh and Tay Khanh Vinh, accounted for 76% of at-risk individuals and all 18 positives; five cases involve children aged 15 or younger. Authorities have launched a 100-day malaria-control plan starting Aug 17 to screen, prevent, and eliminate malaria in 2026, with intensified surveillance in high-risk areas. Preventive teams are deployed through holidays at high-to-very-high risk sites; checkpoints monitor people entering forests. Dr. Ton That Toan, deputy director of the CDC, urges residents to exit forest or fields before 17:00, when Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria most actively. Families should supervise children; those with fever should seek immediate testing rather than self-medicating. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium and is curable with early detection.

triage.headline_ja: カインホア省で新たなマラリア症例が多数検出、医師が対策を助言

article.articleHeadline: Dengue in the Philippines: Increasing trend reported in more than 100 cities
article.articleSummary: Dengue in the Philippines shows an increasing trend across more than 100 cities. From Jan 1 to Aug 29, 2026, 128,634 dengue cases were reported, a 39% decrease from 209,631 in the same period last year. Of these, 48,132 (37%) were laboratory-confirmed, 16,874 (13%) probable, and 63,628 (49%) suspected. Epidemic thresholds were breached at least twice in August in Ilocos Norte (Region I), Aurora (Region III), Albay, Camarines Sur, Camarines Norte, Catanduanes (Region V), Bohol and City of Lapu-Lapu (Region VII), Zamboanga Sibugay and Zamboanga City (Region IX), South Cotabato (Region XII), Basilan, Sulu, BARMM, Abra (CAR), and Agusan del Sur (Caraga). Clustering occurred in 2,760 barangays nationwide, with Region III (299 clusters, 11%), Region VII (277, 10%), and Region I (257, 9%) reporting the most. Total deaths: 510 (CFR 0.04%).

article.articleHeadline: Concurrent Rasmussen aneurysm and pulmonary embolism in a patient with cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: In Canada, a 68-year-old immigrant from the Philippines presented with cough, weight loss and intermittent hemoptysis. Sputum smear was acid-fast positive; MTB PCR was positive and cultures confirmed M. tuberculosis susceptible to first-line drugs. CT showed bilateral upper-lobe cavitations (5 cm left, 4.5 cm right) with tree-in-bud nodularity and right-upper-lobe pulmonary embolism, plus two ~5-mm Rasmussen aneurysms. TB therapy began with isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol; rifampin was switched to rifabutin to permit anticoagulation with apixaban. LMWH was used; after 10 days, small-volume hemoptysis led to withholding anticoagulation and tranexamic acid; CT later showed near-resolution of the PE. Massive hemoptysis occurred; bronchoscopy supported Rasmussen aneurysm bleeding and was controlled with tranexamic acid without embolization or surgery. After 9 months of TB therapy, smear conversion occurred by 2 months and radiographs normalized by 9 months; post-treatment CT showed PE resolution with scarring/bronchiectasis and thrombosis of the feeding vessel upstream of the aneurysms. Contact tracing identified 25 exposed individuals.

article.articleHeadline: In the Irkutsk District, nearly a hundred cows will be culled due to a dermatitis outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Bovine nodular dermatitis (Lumpy Skin Disease) outbreak in Irkutsk Municipal District, Russia. Over 20 infected private farms identified as of 7 September 2026. A cull will destroy 96 cows in the villages of Butyrki and Koty. A state of emergency is declared. Quarantine zones are defined: core zone within 3 km including Oyok, Butyrki, Koty; risk zone within 10 km extending to Khomutovo, Maksimovshchina, Galki, Pozdnyakova, Revykina, Sosnovy Bor, Cheremushka, Zherdovka, Kashtak, Zykova. In Butyrki, grazing is forbidden; movement restricted; meat, milk, and feed transport prohibited. Entrance is limited to local residents and state veterinary staff only. Unscheduled vaccination of livestock is planned in affected areas. Governor Igor Kobzev pledged compensation to farmers for cattle losses. Public health officials emphasize strict quarantine boundaries to prevent spread via transport and people.

All three reportedly originated from North Sumatra, with one of the three still 15 years old. The Health Office (Dinkes Kuansing), led by Helma Muliani, notes the STI outbreak linked to late-night venues closed by Satpol PP-PKP Kuansing. The trio will undergo further medical assessment and treatment. Two adult workers refused repatriation to North Sumatra and chose to stay for treatment in Kuansing, while authorities will ensure the 15-year-old is sent home to her family, who have been contacted. The case highlights STI risks associated with sex work venues in the region.

article.articleHeadline: In Russia, since the beginning of the year, 500 cases of importation of dangerous infections have been detected.
article.articleSummary: Russia registered almost 500 imported cases of dangerous infections in 2026, with no domestic transmission reported, according to Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova. This is up from about 300 imported cases in 2025. The infections cited include malaria, typhoid fever, various fevers, Zika, dengue, and chikungunya. Border controls have been strengthened to prevent domestic spread, with officials saying these cases reflect global instability. In the summer, Rospotrebnadzor urged Russians returning from Bali to monitor health due to dengue, a mosquito-borne viral disease; since the start of the year, more than 100 dengue infections have been identified in Russia. The report emphasizes that these infections are imported and not circulating domestically.

article.articleHeadline: 106 Pigs from Manado Sent to Raja Ampat, Barantin Confirms Negative for African Swine Fever and Foot-and-Mouth Disease
article.articleSummary: 106 live pigs were moved from Manado, North Sulawesi to Raja Ampat, West Papua, after health checks and laboratory tests by Indonesia’s quarantine authorities. Barantan (Badan Karantina Indonesia) via the North Sulawesi Animal, Fish, and Plant Quarantine Office (Karantina Sulut) confirmed on Sept 5, 2026, that samples tested at an accredited lab were negative for African Swine Fever (ASF) and Foot-and-Mouth Disease (PMK). A pre-shipment health assessment and inter-regional risk analysis deemed the shipment’s disease risk controlled, allowing entry into Raja Ampat. Biosecurity steps included disinfection of livestock and transport vehicles. After health clearance, quarantine documents were issued to permit movement, in line with Law No. 21 of 2019 on Animal, Fish, and Plant Quarantine. The measures aim to prevent disease spread and safeguard livestock health in the destination area.

article.articleHeadline: Indonesia Develops an mRNA-Based Dengue Vaccine to Combat the Four Serotypes of the Virus.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia is developing an mRNA-based tetravalent dengue vaccine designed to cover DENV-1 to DENV-4, incorporating local dengue diversity with in silico mutation analysis and AI. The project is a collaboration among Universitas Indonesia (UI), the National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN), LPDP, Etana Biotechnologies Indonesia, and Tsinghua University. At a UI workshop in Depok on August 27–28, 2026, researchers emphasized the need to bridge research to product via scale-up, GMP validation, preclinical/clinical testing, and regulatory pathways, supported by teaching factories that link labs to industry. BPOM’s GROW program provides early regulatory guidance. Early results show the vaccine candidate neutralizes all four serotypes, with some constructs outperforming wild type and Dengvaxia. While promising, further studies are required before clinical use, within a Pentahelix ecosystem and Technology Readiness Level guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Bogor City DPRD Urges City Government to Accelerate Handling of the Surge in HIV Cases
article.articleSummary: Bogor City DPRD warns of a rising HIV burden in Bogor City, urging rapid action. Over the past five years about 2,000 new HIV-positive cases were recorded, including 599 in 2025. The five-year average is roughly 400 per year; about 1,400 people are on antiretroviral therapy. More than 84% of cases involve men (16% women), with most linked to high-risk sexual behaviors, including LGBT. The DPRD calls for accelerated implementation of the P4S Regional Regulation (Pencegahan dan Penanggulangan Penyakit Sosial), stronger public education, and higher funding in the 2027 APBD. They plan to send a letter to the Mayor due to the missing implementing regulation (Perwali). In the meantime, prevention programs—education in schools, families, and communities—should proceed, supported by increased KUA-PPAS funding for early detection and prevention, and youth protection.

Residents claim confiscation of cattle, including visibly healthy animals, while laboratory tests have not yet confirmed the disease. Officials say measures follow a plan by the regional veterinary service and urge residents to cooperate. One farm owner in the villages of Oyok, Butyrki and Koty reportedly attempted suicide amid the slaughter and was hospitalized. Veterinarian Svetlana Shchepetkina suggested symptoms could indicate foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) and noted that protective gear was not changed between diseased and healthy farms during inspections. The incident echoes a similar mass-slaughter controversy earlier this year in Novosibirsk Oblast, where authorities cited dangerous infections but farmers contested the extent of culling.

article.articleHeadline: Be on alert for Singapore flu transmission in Malinau as the Health Office tightens surveillance of health facilities.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 September 2026, Malinau Regency's Health Office in East Kalimantan instructs all health facilities to tighten surveillance for Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD), commonly called Singapore flu. The focus is on preventing transmission to children under 10, and avoiding a materially epidemiological outbreak (KLB). The plan assigns tasks: primary clinics (puskesmas) trace active cases; hospitals stand by to treat severe patients. Transmission occurs easily via close contact, droplets from coughing or sneezing, and contaminated surfaces, with daily child-activity settings such as households, daycare, and schools identified as high-risk. Recognize symptoms: fever, painful oral ulcers, difficulty eating/drinking, followed by vesicles or red spots on hands and feet. Parents should not bring symptomatic toddlers to Posyandu; sick children should stay home and seek medical care promptly.

article.articleHeadline: Getting to Know Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Bacillus cereus that can cause food poisoning
article.articleSummary: On February 12, 2024, 59 students at SMK Muhammadiyah 3 Gemolong, Sragen, Central Java, suffered food poisoning after snacks were shared to 330 pupils during a gathering; items included bottled water, arem-arem, and cake. Hygiene issues—staff not wearing gloves or reusing gloves—were cited as exposure risks. The report notes that Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Bacillus cereus are common food-poisoning culprits, widespread in the environment and humans, with some strains causing illness directly or via toxins. E. coli strains (ETEC, EHEC/STEC, UPEC) can be contracted from contaminated meat, raw vegetables, or unpasteurized dairy, or via contact with animals or contaminated surroundings. Symptoms can include urinary tract infection signs such as painful urination and fever. References include GOV.UK/FSA and a 2025 BMC Infectious Diseases study.

article.articleHeadline: Scrub typhus bacteria found in chiggers and ground birds
article.articleSummary: Scrub typhus, caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, sickens tens of thousands annually in the Asia-Pacific. A Malaysia–UK–Thailand study provides the first convincing molecular hints that ground-dwelling birds can carry Orientia-related material and that bird-associated chiggers may harbor related genetic elements. Across 14 sites in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, chiggers were collected from red junglefowl, domestic chickens, and rails; pools were screened for the htrA gene by nested PCR and a subset underwent Illumina metagenomic sequencing. Validation with infected Leptotrombidium chiangraiensis chiggers showed near-complete Orientia genome recovery, confirming method viability. In field samples, most chigger pools from birds were negative by both approaches. One pool of Blankaartia acuscutellaris from Lewinia striata yielded Orientia-related contigs but could not assemble core genes, leaving infection unconfirmed. Ongoing evidence in bird tissues showed O. tsutsugamushi DNA in one red junglefowl and one domestic chicken, suggesting potential exposure or carriage and a possible new dimension to scrub typhus ecology.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza tops Phuket communicable disease
article.articleSummary: Week 35 surveillance at Vachira Phuket Hospital shows 347 reported communicable-disease cases, led by influenza with 119 cases and one death; acute diarrhoea (68), COVID-19 (64), pneumonia (35) and dengue fever (16) complete the top five. These five conditions account for 302 of the week’s cases; the remaining 45 involve other monitored diseases such as RSV, hand-foot-and-mouth disease, syphilis, gonorrhoea, acute hepatitis B, conjunctivitis, scarlet fever, chickenpox and food poisoning. Among 347 patients, 161 were male and 186 female. Geographically, Mueang Phuket District bore 243 cases, followed by Thalang (53) and Kathu (40); 11 cases originated from other provinces. Separate surveillance for dangerous communicable diseases found no PUI, no confirmed cases, and no deaths during the week; the influenza death is included in the overall counts. Ongoing weekly surveillance and a dashboard are used for feedback.

article.articleHeadline: In Russia, 500 cases of imported dangerous infections were recorded — Evening Kazan.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-09-07, Russia recorded 500 imported infectious-disease cases this year, with none resulting in local transmission, according to Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova. The imports span malaria, typhoid fever, a range of fevers, as well as Zika, dengue, and chikungunya. Despite the variety of pathogens, implemented countermeasures have prevented spread, and border controls have been strengthened to form a robust 'sanitary shield.' By contrast, last year saw 300 imported cases. Popova noted a globally unsettled epidemiological situation. In summer, Russia also identified an imported case of melioidosis in a tourist from Thailand, with the patient hospitalized in serious condition. The report underscores heightened vigilance at points of entry and ongoing public-health measures to avert international-to-local transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Apply for Community-Based TB Prevention and Care (Ghana) - fundsforNGOs
article.articleSummary: UNICEF Ghana seeks a qualified CSO/NGO to strengthen community-based TB prevention, screening, contact tracing, referral, and linkage to care in high-burden areas of Ghana, in collaboration with the National TB Control Programme. The initiative targets earlier TB identification, diagnostic completion, and timely treatment, with emphasis on children, household contacts, and underserved populations facing access barriers. Objectives include expanding community TB awareness, targeted screening, presumptive case identification, enhanced contact tracing, referral to diagnostics, completion of diagnostic processes, and linkage to treatment, plus documentation of lessons for scale-up. Activities cover community education, screening, identification of presumptive TB, household contact tracing, referral and follow-up, and ensuring confidentiality while coordinating with TB and health-system stakeholders. The program aims to strengthen the full pathway from community awareness to diagnosis and care, reducing delays and missed opportunities in Ghana's high-burden settings.

article.articleHeadline: Cholera and AWD: Reemergence in Yangon, Myanmar and elsewhere
article.articleSummary: Cholera and acute watery diarrhea (AWD) have reemerged in Yangon, Myanmar, and neighboring regions, according to the UN Health Cluster led by the WHO. As of Aug 31, 2026, cases are reported in Yangon and across western Rakhine’s Sittwe, eastern Mon, and central Ayeyarwady, echoing 2024 outbreaks. In Yangon, 750+ cholera/AWD cases were documented from Aug 1–22, with more than 300 severe; by Aug 18, about 500 hospitalizations and roughly 150 cholera positives, with at least one death. Sittwe recorded over 150 cases, about half severe, and four deaths. Mon State has four cases, two recently visiting AWD areas in Yangon. Flooding affects Sagaing (16 townships), Magway (four), Ayeyarwady (three), with AWD emerging in these flood-impacted zones, affecting 470,000+ people. Malaria and dengue are rising; shortages of bed nets and other supplies are reported in eastern Kayah, southern Tanintharyi, northern Kachin, western Chin, and Sagaing.
